label: text
text: WANCHAI GAP HOUSE.

label: text
text: Regarded Plan As "Scrap Of Paper."

label: text
text: The question of what was a reasonable amount for an architect to charge for preparing a sketch plan of a house it was proposed to erect at Wanchai Gap arose out of a case before Mr. Justice Wood in the Summary Court. this morning.

label: text
text: Mr. H. H. Bourne, architect, of Prince's "Building, claimed $900 from Mr. N. V. A. Croucher, broken, of Messrs. Benjamin and Potts, for services rendered. The claim was made up of items for "taking instructions, preparing a sketch design and making approximate estimate of cost by public measurement, or otherwise for a house to be built at or near Wanchai Gap." The claim was based on 1½ per cent. on the approximated cost of house ($60,000).

label: text
text: Mr. H. C. Macnamara was for plaintiff and Mr. M. M. Watson for the defendant.

label: text
text: Mr. Macnamara, in opening, said that defendant had paid $150 into court but plaintiff was unable to accept it as it was totally inadequate.

label: text
text: In June of last year, said Mr. Macnamara, Mr. Croucher contemplated having a house built on an eminence near Wanchai Gap. He had been in negotiations with the Government to buy a certain plot of land and the land had subsequently been bought by him.

label: paragraph_title
text: A. Sketch Plan.

label: text
text:
Mr. Macnamara detailed interviews between the parties and Mr. Newhouse, of the P.W.D. It would serve no good purpose to call the latter, he remarked as Mr. Newhouse had stated that certain matters which they (plaintiffs) said had been referred to in his presence had slipped his mind. On July 28 of last year Mr. Croucher gave Mr. Bourne instructions to draw up a preliminary sketch plan which was to show the sort of house Mr. Croucher wanted, Mr. Croucher having detailed his requirements.
When the parties met again on August 6, continued Mr. Macnamara, matters had so far progressed that Mr. L. C. P. Rees had actually put pegs on the land to show the boundaries, Mr. Bourne had drawn two plans and discussion took place on them. One was more elaborate showing estimated cost of erection as $60,000. The other plan was for a house, estimated cost of erection $50,000. Although Mr. Croucher thought that $60,000 was rather more than he wished to pay he preferred the first plan to the second and took it away with him. He had had it from that time to the present, said Mr. Macnamara.

label: text
text: In the following month, continued Mr. Macnamara, Mr. Bourne had an interview with Mr. Croucher in which the latter said that he was not "quite sure whether he would authorise the building to go on at once yet he wanted the working drawings of the plans made out." He gave Mr. Bourne instructions accordingly.

label: paragraph_title
text: Correspondence.

label: text
text: Letters between the parties were read, the first being that from Mr. Bourne to Mr. Croucher following the last interview referred to. Mr. Bourne said he would proceed at once with the drawing and specifications and would submit further sketch drawings of plans and elevation before the work was too far advanced. On completion he would give an estimate of cost. The letter further stated that the architect's fees would be 5 per cent. of the estimated cost of building and an additional 2 per cent. when everything was ready for the building to proceed.

label: text
text: In his reply the following day, Mr. Croucher said that he and Mrs. Croucher had been talking the matter over and they had decided that it would be better to wait a little longer before definitely committing themselves to the building. Mr. Potts would be returning from England shortly, and it was possible that any plans previously made might be upset. The letter stated that it was Mr. Croucher's intention to

label: text
text: DETECTED BY POLICE

label: text
text: A traffic officer's memory brought to earth a Chinese who was trying to obtain, a motor car driver's licence by marking a secret of his past.

label: text
text: The man had in the usual course informed Sergeant Baker that he had not held a licence before and was being tested as to his fitness when Sub-Inspector Alexander recognised him as a driver whose licence had been cancelled in 1922 for reckless driving.

label: text
text: When charged before Major C. Willson at the Central Magistracy this morning with falling to inform the police that his licence had been cancelled when applying for a new one, the man denied that he was questioned on this point. This plea failed to satisfy His Worship, who imposed a fine of $25.

label: text
text: CHANG'S ATTITUDE.

label: text
text: M. Borodin, the Russian high adviser to the Canton Government, is once gain in the line-light.

label: text
text: According to a Chinese report, he is reported to have asked what is meant by the alleged, proposed alliance between General Chang Kai-shek (commander-in-chief of Kwangtung) and Marshal Sun Chuan-fang (Tupan of Kiangsu, Chekiang and Fukien).

label: text
text: Marshall Sun is virtually warlord of the lower Yangtsze valley and that part of the south China coast excepting Kwangtung. His domains adjoin the sphere of the Nationalist Government in Canton. He has been reported to be seeking an alliance with General Chang Kai-shek, while other sources emphasise his allegiance to Wu Pei-fu.

label: text
text: At a meeting of the General Council of the Kuomintang, M. Borodin, and a Chinese member, are said to have alleged that General Chang had secretly despatched emissaries to interview Marshal Sun and the governor of Szechuan. Words attributed to M. Borodin and his Chinese colleague are that a cable was received from the Kuomintang branch in Kiangsu that cadets from the Whampoa Military Academy had been sent North; also that a similar message had been sent from Szechuan province.

label: text
text: It was resolved to hand the matter over to general (military) headquarters and the Whampoa Academy for investigation and report.

label: text

label: text
text: STAFF DIFFICULTIES.

label: text
text: Canton Strike Has An Indirect

label: text
text: A department of the local public service which receives little publicity except when the annual report of its working is published is that concerned with the Post Office administration. Yet, needless to say, the work of sorting, delivery and transhipment and the supervision and administration proceeds daily — sometimes nightly—with demands on the time and labour of the whole department particularly heavy at certain times.

label: text
text: A correspondent to-day refers rather "belatedly to delay in the delivery of newspapers arriving on Saturday morning and received on Monday holding that if the department is under-staffed steps should be taken to make up the deficiency.

label: text
text: A “China Mail” representative who made enquiries was informed that the delay referred to was on account of the staff having to prepare for an outward mail to Europe on the day in question as well as two inward Europe mails and other smaller mails both ways. As it was the end of the month, some 200 men had had to be paid, this also leading to a certain amount of interruption.

label: text
text: For normal times the present staff of the Post Office is sufficient, he was further informed, although the especial difficulties faced by men who were comparatively new to the work had to be taken into consideration. A large percentage of the clerical and outdoor staff consisted of men engaged since the strike and although they were doing their best it stood to reason that they were not yet as conversant with the technicalities as men who had been engaged on the work for ten years or more (as some of the men who left during the strike had been). A great deal of extra supervision work was required. A Record July.

label: text
text: Further interesting facts with regard to the amount of mail handled by the department were given to the newspaper representative. Hongkong acts as a sort of “Clapham Junction” in regard to transhipment of mail in the Orient and transhipment involves a considerable “and growing” demand on the time of certain of the employees owing to fewer ships going direct from Shanghai to Canton since the strike and the growing use of the postal service in regard to communications between those ports and between Shanghai and Yunnan.

label: text
text:
This will be more fully appreciated when it is stated that during July of this year over 21,000 bags of mail were received here, this number being a record for one month within the memory of members of the staff who can go back over many years.
Considerable extra work has had to be undertaken as an indirect outcome of the Canton strike, mails which have been transhipped to boats for Canton having to be brought back in certain cases, unloaded and transferred to other boats. Although Shanghai has been cabled with regard to the impossibility of parcels to Canton being handled by the depleted staff there, a considerable number had had to be stored here which had left there prior to the notification.

label: text
text: The Siberian route, it would appear from further answers to the "China Mail" representative's enquiries, is being very extensively used at the present time particularly for the despatch of newspapers and periodicals, from Europe here, although, naturally enough, the quantity despatched from here via that route is considerably less. The opening up of the Tientsin-Pochow railway enabling mail for North China and Europe via Siberia to be forwarded to Harbin by the rail route had enabled the local authorities to make more regular air reliable connections in Shanghai.
